newsitem.title: USA: Opinion Research sees net below expected.
newsitem.headline: Opinion Research sees net below expected.

text.p: Opinion Research Corp said Tuesday it expects earnings per share for the third and fourth quarters of 1996 to be substantially lower than originally anticipated.
The company said third quarter earnings per share are expected to be $0.02-$0.04, with continuing low performance through the fourth quarter.

Opinion Research commented: "The absence of anticipated EPS performance in the second half of 1996 is primarily due to delays in the award of significant new multi-year contracts expected from a major existing client."
The company said it has made significant investments in anticipation of these new contracts.
It said the second half will also reflect "GSR Group transition issues associated with the replacement of the GSR Group CEO in London.

"While we are disappointed with the impact of these matters on the company's anticipated results, we believe they are transitory in nature and that the company's core business is healthy," its statement continued.
"In addition, while the company is currently behind schedule in completing acquisitions, there are a number of acquisition candidates with whom we are currently in discussion.

"These companies meet our EPS-additive requirements and we expect that they will enhance and accelerate implementation of the company's strategy. If completed, such acquisitions will further strengthen the revenue growth and profit performance of the company over time," Opinion Research said.
